title: ROLLUP, CUBE, and GROUPING SETS
description: Produce subtotals and grand totals in one pass and label them so NULL is not ambiguous.

data.text: A sales report needs revenue by region and category, plus a subtotal per region, plus a grand total — all in one result set. A `NULL` in the region column already means "unknown region" in the data, so it cannot also mean "subtotal". Write the query and disambiguate the totals.

data.title: SQL Solution
data.code:
-- ROLLUP: hierarchical subtotals — (Region, Category), (Region), ()
SELECT
    CASE WHEN GROUPING(Region)   = 1 THEN 'ALL REGIONS'  ELSE Region   END AS Region,
    CASE WHEN GROUPING(Category) = 1 THEN 'ALL CATEGORIES' ELSE Category END AS Category,
    SUM(Amount) AS Revenue,
    GROUPING(Region) AS IsRegionSubtotal
FROM Sales
GROUP BY ROLLUP (Region, Category)
ORDER BY Region, Category;

-- CUBE: every combination — adds (Category) subtotals as well
SELECT
    Region,
    Category,
    SUM(Amount) AS Revenue
FROM Sales
GROUP BY CUBE (Region, Category);

-- GROUPING SETS: exactly the aggregates you need, no more
SELECT
    Region,
    Category,
    SUM(Amount) AS Revenue
FROM Sales
GROUP BY GROUPING SETS (
    (Region, Category),   -- detail
    (Region),             -- subtotal per region
    ()                    -- grand total
);

data.title: Explanation
data.text: The `GROUPING()` function returns **1** when the column was rolled up (i.e. the `NULL` is a placeholder) and **0** when it is a genuine data value — this is the only reliable way to tell a subtotal from a real `NULL`. `ROLLUP (Region, Category)` produces totals in the order given: region+category detail, then region subtotal, then grand total. `CUBE` generates every permutation, which is usually more than a report needs. `GROUPING SETS` is the precise tool: you list exactly the aggregates required, so you pay only for those. All three are implemented as a single pass over the data, which is far cheaper than three separate `UNION ALL` queries with `GROUP BY`.
